messages:
kevin: Hey team — I need to add my adult sibling (disabled) to my medical + dental. He's 28, US citizen, currently living with me part-time in Spain (rotating 6 months). SSN application is in progress (no SSN yet). What docs do you need and can coverage start retro to 2026-08-01?

michelle (People Ops): Hi Kevin — short answer: we can start the process pending SSN but we need specific docs. For adult disabled dependents we require: 1) proof of disability (SSA award letter OR physician statement), 2) proof of dependency/financial support, and 3) identity docs (passport) and residence evidence if living abroad. SSN usually required but we allow provisional enrollment while SSN is pending. Is he a US citizen (you said yes?) and is the residence permanent or intermittent?

kevin: Yes, US citizen with valid passport. Residence is intermittent — he stays with me several months each year. SSN app submitted, should be processed in a few weeks. I missed the 30-day QLE window though — he moved in 2026-08-01. Can we still get retro coverage?

ana (typo)

ana (Benefits) [edited to ana (Benefits)]: Ana: We can enroll pending SSN if you submit the signed affidavit and documentation within 90 days of enrollment. For retro to 2026-08-01: standard rule is QLE within 30 days. However exceptions are considered for international delays or administrative issues. Please submit the "Late-dependent-add exception" form with all supporting docs and a short explanation of the delay.

kevin: Got it. What counts as acceptable "proof of dependency"? He receives SSDI; I pay rent and share expenses. Also, for foreign docs — does the physician statement need an apostille or is a certified translation ok?

ana (Benefits): Acceptable dependency proof: shared lease, bank transfers showing support, joint utility bills, or a signed financial support affidavit. SSDI/SSDI award letter is helpful too. For foreign medical docs: certified translation is fine; apostille only if authenticity is in question. Make sure translations include translator contact and date.

people-ops-bot: File: /hr/forms/late-dependent-exception.pdf (fillable). Submit it and upload docs to Workday under Benefits > Documentation. Link: https://redwood-internal/hr/forms/dependent-exception

raj (Payroll): If approved retro, payroll will recalculate premiums back to the effective date. We need final SSN within 90 days; if not provided, we may reverse the retro premium adjustments. HSA note: adding an adult dependent doesn't change individual HSA eligibility rules; check with Benefits if you're on a family plan vs individual.

kevin: Understood. I'll compile: passport, SSDI award, physician statement (translated), proof of shared expenses, and the exception form.

kevin: Quick Q on filenames — is there a preferred name when uploading?

michelle (People Ops): any clear filename is fine, e.g., `kevin_late-dep-exception_2026-09.pdf`. Put all docs in one upload if possible.

kevin: Uploaded: late-dependent-exception.pdf, physician-translation.pdf, ssdi_award.pdf, proof_of_support.pdf to Workday just now.

michelle (People Ops): Received. We'll review and aim to respond within 5 business days. If we need anything else we'll ping you here. :thumbsup: 

kevin: Thanks so much — appreciate the help :pray:

michelle (People Ops): Filing note: If approved we'll notify Payroll and Benefits to execute retro enrollment and adjust premiums. Keep an eye on Workday tasks for the SSN update.

kevin: Will do, thanks!
